key_insight: LLM embeddings complemented theory-driven language features and cognitive scores, with an any-positive ensemble improving prediction of APOE4 carrier status and amyloid-beta burden.
clinical_relevance: Picture-description language may support future noninvasive screening research for Alzheimer’s-related risk and pathology, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Analyzed Cookie Theft picture descriptions from Hebrew- and English-speaking cohorts.
Compared pretrained LLM embeddings, theory-driven linguistic features, and cognitive test scores.
Combined predictions using an any-positive ensemble and evaluated multiple amyloid-beta cutoffs.
evidence_signal: Across IRAP (N=134) and WRAP (N=1,541), the ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline on all 8 APOE4/global amyloid-beta tasks, and all constituent models on 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks.
watch_item: An any-positive ensemble may increase false positives; specificity and prospective clinical performance require validation before screening use.
paper_title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
